title: cold-start-rehydration-and-tfstate-sync-playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook documents a tested cold-start disaster recovery (DR) and state rehydration procedure for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It focuses on: full-system reconstitution after a site failure, tfstate synchronization patterns for multi-admin teams, Terraform module considerations to avoid data loss during upgrades, and a verification checklist for post-restore validation.

Audience and assumptions:
- Audience: SREs, platform engineers, and solutions engineers who execute restores or run DR drills.
- Assumes: cluster control plane may be unavailable; we have access to object-store snapshots, database backups, and an offsite copy of Terraform state. Network access to customer VPC or on-prem recovery network is available via a jump host. Operators have encryption key access (KMS/HSM) for snapshot decryption.

RTO/RPO targets and decision matrix:
- Tier-1 API endpoints: target RTO 1 hour (when Dedicated capacity available), RPO 15 minutes (if WAL shipping enabled).
- Admin consoles and non-critical batch processes: RTO 6 hours, RPO 24 hours.
- If only cold backups exist (last nightly snapshot), escalate to business leads and follow cold-start script.

High-level recovery phases:
1) Mobilize & validate authorizations
   - Confirm incident channel, assemble DR lead, infra lead, DB lead, security lead.
   - Verify access to offsite artifact bucket and Terraform state bucket.
2) Recover control plane and networking
   - Recreate minimal networking (VPC/subnets/route tables) using the terraform module: network/recovery (see Terraform notes below).
   - Ensure BGP/VPN or transit connectivity to customer jump host is established.
3) Restore persistent stores in order of dependency
   - Object storage (model shards, cached artifacts)
   - Key-value stores (Redis/Ephemeral cache restored as empty or filled via rehydration depending on RPO)
   - Databases (Postgres/Cockroach): restore from WAL + base snapshot or point-in-time where available
   - Message queues (Kafka/Rabbit): restore topic offsets if stored snapshot available
4) Rehydrate stateful services and model runtime
   - Deploy statefulsets with PVs bound to restored volumes; start services in read-only mode until verification complete
5) Run application-level data migrations and health checks
   - Perform smoke traffic through canary hosts, validate end-to-end inference path including token-level tracing and KV-cache hit rates
6) Scale to steady-state and run post-mortem

Terraform & tfstate notes (critical):
- Always keep a write-protected offsite tfstate: s3://redwood-offsite-tfstate/<customer>/ (server-side encryption + kms) with versioning enabled.
- Use state locking (dynamodb or equivalent) for active restores to prevent concurrent applies.
- When performing a cold-start, use terraform init -migrate-state with the recovery backend pointing to the offsite bucket and set TF_VAR_recovery=true to select recovery module variants.
- Terraform module design recommendations to minimize blast radius:
  - network module: expose a boolean variable recovery_mode that allows safe recreation of only required subnets and route tables; avoid destroying customer-managed resources by using lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } on critical resources (e.g., customer's customer-managed keys, onprem VPN endpoints).
  - storage module: separate lifecycle for snapshot lifecycle rules and restored PVs; restored PVs should be created via explicit data sources referencing the offsite snapshot ID rather than relying on automated recreation.
  - database module: avoid automated resource replacement on scheme drift during recovery; expose a controlled upgrade toggle (db_autoupgrade = false) for DR.
- Tfstate synchronization pattern: when an operator recovers into a secondary region or air-gapped site, perform a dry-run plan against the recovered backend, review diffs, then apply with -target flags to bring up the minimal set of resources.

Snapshot catalog & naming convention:
- Offsite snapshots use ISO timestamp + cluster-id + tool tags: e.g., 2024-08-21T03-24-12Z_cluster-03_postgres-base-snap.enc
- Maintain a snapshot index file in the offsite bucket: snapshot-index.csv with fields: snapshot_id, resource_type, created_at, encryption_tag, ttl_days. During a restore, operators grep the index to find the most recent consistent snapshot set.

Step-by-step cold-start runbook (play-by-play):
1) Triage and initial artifact retrieval (0–30m)
   - Confirm DR run: post message in #drill-ops and create ephemeral DR channel.
   - Export current offsite snapshot-index.csv and lock tfstate (dynamodb lock + tag called dr-lock).
   - Copy required snapshots to the recovery bucket under recovery/<incident-id>/ with SSE-KMS.
2) Networking and DNS (30–60m)
   - terraform workspace select recovery; terraform apply -target=module.network -var="recovery_mode=true" -auto-approve
   - Update DNS entries in Route53 or internal DNS to point to recovery load-balancers (or configure hosts file for initial smoke tests).
3) Storage & DB restore (60–180m)
   - Restore object-store by restoring the snapshot tarball into minio or customer S3-compatible endpoint. Verify object counts and checksums (sha256).
   - For Postgres: restore basebackup -> apply WALs. If WALs missing, fall back to latest full snapshot and mark data as potentially stale.
   - Verify DB logical consistency: run integrity SQL checks (row counts for critical tables, foreign key counts, sample queries).
4) Stateful services bring-up (180–240m)
   - Apply terraform -target for relevant statefulsets. Use image tag pinned to last-known-good.
   - Start services in a gradient: model-serving runtime -> router -> api -> console.
5) System validation and smoke traffic (240–360m)
   - Run smoke-test suite (see linked artifacts) against canary endpoints. Validate token latency distribution and model outputs on a small prompt set.
   - Validate telemetry: metrics pipeline, logs, and tracing. Ensure cost accounting tags are present.
6) Cutover and scaling (360m+)
   - Once canaries pass, move traffic progressively. Release tfstate lock and promote the recovery backend to primary if required.

Upgrade considerations during or after restore:
- Never run schema-changing Terraform applies as part of initial restore unless explicitly planned. Use separate upgrade runs post-restore with a staged plan and a migration window.
- For major runtime upgrades, pin runtime image and kernel optimizations until after traffic baseline is validated.
- Document any module drift between offsite tfstate and current module versions. Prefer stabilizing module code to match tfstate then run a controlled module upgrade.

Verification checklist (items to sign off):
- Control plane reachable and kubectl context stable
- PVs bound and checksummed against snapshot manifest
- Databases restored to target LSN or snapshot id (documented)
- Message queue topics present and offsets in range
- Canary inference latency p50/p95 within expected thresholds
- Token accounting and cost telemetry emitting
- Audit logs and KMS access logs intact

Post-restore housekeeping:
- Push recovered tfstate snapshot to central offsite with new version tag and rotate access keys used for recovery.
- Create a post-mortem ticket with timeline, root cause hypothesis, and action items.
- Run a reconstruction drill within 30 days to validate improvements.

Playbook appendix: quick commands and snippets
- Lock tfstate: aws dynamodb put-item --table-name tfstate-locks --item '{"LockID": {"S": "<customer>-dr-<id>"}}'
- Terraform recovery init (example): terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-offsite-tfstate" -backend-config="key=<customer>/recovery.tfstate"
- Postgres restore example: pg_basebackup -D /var/lib/postgresql/data -R -X stream -S <slot> -h <wal-host> -U repl_user
- Checksum objects: find /data/minio -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; > manifest.sha256

Open questions and risks to track in retro:
- Partial WAL retention policies for customers on tight retention windows; need standardized WAL shipping defaults.
- Tests for tfmodule prevent_destroy semantics on customer-managed resources across provider versions.
- Automating verification of model shard integrity when using incremental shard uploads.

Related references and follow-ups:
- Follow-up tickets: ENG-DR-567 (automate snapshot-index generation), ENG-OPS-598 (tfmodule recovery_mode refactor).
- Ownership: SRE lead (Ethan Chen) owns drill scheduling; Platform eng (Nadia Brooks) owns tfmodule changes; Solutions eng triages customer-specific network configs.

Revision history:
- 2024-08-21 initial draft
- 2024-11-02 added tfstate sync patterns and naming convention
- 2025-03-11 expanded verification checklist and snippet examples

Notes to operators:
Keep this doc intentionally prescriptive but adaptable. During a live DR, communicate constantly, minimize concurrent terraform operations, and err on the side of data preservation (prevent_destroy and explicit restores). When in doubt, escalate to the platform lead.
